title: Make repo marker files sensitive to repo mapping changes

timeline.message:
Make repo marker files sensitive to repo mapping changes

Similar to the fix for https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20721, we write recorded repo mapping entries into the marker file so that repo fetching is sensitive to any relevant repo mapping changes.

Fixes #20722.
timeline.author: Xùdōng Yáng

diff.patch:
@@ -2615,4 +2615,93 @@ EOF
   assert_contains 'WORKSPACE' output
 }
 
+function test_repo_mapping_change_in_rule_impl() {
+  # regression test for #20722
+  create_new_workspace
+  cat > MODULE.bazel <<EOF
+r = use_repo_rule("//:r.bzl", "r")
+r(name = "r")
+bazel_dep(name="foo", repo_name="data")
+local_path_override(module_name="foo", path="foo")
+bazel_dep(name="bar")
+local_path_override(module_name="bar", path="bar")
+EOF
+  touch BUILD
+  cat > r.bzl <<EOF
+def _r(rctx):
+  print("I see: " + str(Label("@data")))
+  rctx.file("BUILD", "filegroup(name='r')")
+r=repository_rule(_r)
+EOF
+  mkdir foo
+  cat > foo/MODULE.bazel <<EOF
+module(name="foo")
+EOF
+  mkdir bar
+  cat > bar/MODULE.bazel <<EOF
+module(name="bar")
+EOF
+
+  bazel build @r >& $TEST_log || fail "expected bazel to succeed"
+  expect_log "I see: @@foo~override//:data"
+
+  # So far, so good. Now we make `@data` point to bar instead!
+  cat > MODULE.bazel <<EOF
+r = use_repo_rule("//:r.bzl", "r")
+r(name = "r")
+bazel_dep(name="foo")
+local_path_override(module_name="foo", path="foo")
+bazel_dep(name="bar", repo_name="data")
+local_path_override(module_name="bar", path="bar")
+EOF
+  # for the repo `r`, nothing except the repo mapping has changed.
+  bazel build @r >& $TEST_log || fail "expected bazel to succeed"
+  expect_log "I see: @@bar~override//:data"
+}
+
+function test_repo_mapping_change_in_bzl_init() {

+  mkdir foo

+module(name="foo")
+EOF
+  mkdir bar

+  bazel build @r >& $TEST_log || fail "expected bazel to succeed"

+  # So far, so good. Now we make `@data` point to bar instead!
+  cat > MODULE.bazel <<EOF
+r = use_repo_rule("//:r.bzl", "r")
+r(name = "r")
+bazel_dep(name="foo")
+local_path_override(module_name="foo", path="foo")
+bazel_dep(name="bar", repo_name="data")
+local_path_override(module_name="bar", path="bar")
+EOF
+  # for the repo `r`, nothing except the repo mapping has changed.
+  bazel build @r >& $TEST_log || fail "expected bazel to succeed"

timeline.body:
Similar to the fix for https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/20721, we write recorded repo mapping entries into the marker file so that repo fetching is sensitive to any relevant repo mapping changes.

Fixes #20722.
Not directly related, but the comment on line 110 sounds pretty scary. Could you check on the details of the internal bug?

reply.body: I have; the linked bug focuses on a different topic. I think it shouldn't matter for repo rules used in bzlmod anyway, which have to be exported symbols and thus cannot close over anything lower in the call stack.

actually, this _is_ a problem: I talked to @brandjon about this, and he explained to me what's wrong here. Imagine the following:

```starlark
# foo.bzl
def make_repo_rule(impl):
    return repository_rule(impl)

# bar.bzl
load(":foo.bzl", "make_repo_rule")
def _my_rule_impl(rctx):
   # ...
my_rule = make_repo_rule(_my_rule_impl)
```

With the current code, the "transitive bzl digest" of `my_rule` is actually the transitive bzl digest of `foo.bzl`, since that's where the `repository_rule()` call happens. What we _should_ obviously be using is `bar.bzl`, which is actually at the bottom of the call stack. In order to do that, line 112 should simply be grabbing the information from the corresponding BzlInitThreadContext (née BazelStarlarkContext). I'll send a separate fix for this.

In any case, this PR itself is not affected; we're already using the "repo mapping recorder" from the "bottom of the call stack", since there's only one recorder for the entire thread, not one per call stack frame.
actually, you know what... I'll just fix it in this PR.

gaah.. I reverted the fix. The reason is that we current allow usage of unexported repo rules in WORKSPACE, like:

```starlark
# foo.bzl
def foo()
    abc = repository_rule(...)
    abc(name="def")

# WORKSPACE
load(":foo.bzl", "foo")
foo()
```

In this case, there is no BzlInitThreadContext for us to work with, since the "bottom of the stack" is literally the WORKSPACE file itself.

So properly fixing this TODO would break WORKSPACE usage. I'll send a separate change to gate the fix behind `--noenable_workspace` instead.

Gating a correctness fix behind a flag that most users won't flip for another year or so isn't ideal.

I would expect unexported repo rules to be quite rare. Couldn't we default to using the outermost bzl context and fall back to the innermost if the outermost one is WORKSPACE?
hmm, that's true. We can check for existence of BzlInitThreadContext. If it exists, do the proper thing; otherwise, fall back to the current wrong behavior. Will address in another change anyway.

timeline.body: Can this be part of StarlarkThread instead? Doing thread locals this way is "action at a distance" and makes it impossible to track down what other code this affects.

reply.body:
as in, you want the repo mapping recorder itself to be built into StarlarkThread? But StarlarkThread is part of the interpreter and has no concept of repo mappings or labels.

Also, I wouldn't say it's 'impossible' to track down -- it's as easy as finding all usages of `Label.RepoMappingRecorder.class`.
I was about to say "but at least use `StarlarkThread.setThreadLocal()`,but that's not conceptually much different than just a regular thread local, so meh.
not too sure what you mean, but I _am_ using `StarlarkThread#setThreadLocal()` :)

timeline.body: What happens if you downgrade your Bazel version to something that does not understand this new tag?

reply.body: the marker file version was incremented.
Ow, my bad. It indeed was.

timeline.body: Is this in some canonical order?

reply.body: yes, it's sorted. see impl of `recordedEntries`
